summary.headline: Keystone Realtors FY26 presales rose 33% to INR4,022 crore, with FY27 presales guided at INR5,000 crore and a INR10,000 crore presales target by FY30.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q4 presales of INR1,346 crore (up 58% YoY) and full-year presales of INR4,022 crore (up 33%), about 1.74x its BD guidance. Revenue from operations was INR1,596 crore in Q4 and INR2,635 crore for FY26, with OCF of about INR715 crore. The company transitioned from completion method to percentage-of-completion accounting from 1 April 2025, and management says legacy low-margin projects are largely behind it. Gross debt was INR755 crore at March 2026 (gross D/E 0.26:1), and CRISIL assigned AA- with stable outlook.

segments.name: Residential sales and launches
segments.commentary: Seven projects launched in FY26 with GDV of INR9,813 crore (1.4x INR7,000 crore guidance); two launched in Q4 with GDV INR3,978 crore. Of FY26 presales, INR1,620 crore came from new launches and INR2,400 crore from the opening pipeline.

segments.name: Business development
segments.commentary: Five projects added in FY26 with GDV of INR10,400 crore (1.74x INR6,000 crore guidance). Since FY23, 25 projects worth over INR27,800 crore added, 21 of them redevelopment; each underwritten at about 35% gross margin with equity capped near 10% of GDV.

segments.name: Legacy projects (Crown, Virar affordable)
segments.commentary: Legacy projects were 62% of FY26 revenue and are guided to 12% in FY27. Crown has about INR180 crore inventory and about INR450 crore sold receivables, with exit expected by December 2026.

segments.name: Commercial annuity
segments.commentary: Target of about INR100 crore recurring rental income by 2030. Current assets are 33Fifteen (strata sales underway), a 2 million sq ft Thane project (phases of 4.5 lakh sq ft, expected next FY), and Dhuruwadi in Prabhadevi.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales guidance INR5,000 crore (about 25% growth); FY27 project launches about INR8,000 crore; acquisitions about INR8,000-plus crore.
Target of INR10,000 crore presales by FY30, requiring about 26% CAGR from FY27.
FY27 OCF expected a little over INR1,000 crore (FY26: about INR700-715 crore).
Gross debt-to-equity to be capped at 0.75:1. Peak gross debt guided at INR1,300-1,400 crore in FY27 (excluding commercial); FY28 peak to be discussed later.
FY27 finance cost estimated at about INR95 crore (average debt about INR1,000 crore at 9.5%).
Revenue recognition under percentage-of-completion: about 40% completion method, 60% POCM in FY27; 100% POCM from FY28. Revenue acceleration expected from FY28.
Collection efficiency expected at 75-80% from this year onwards.
Blended gross margin of about 35% and EBITDA of about 20% on current projects; affordable/mid-size tends toward 30% gross margin and luxury toward 40%.
capex_capacity: Construction spend rose to INR997 crore in FY26 from INR829 crore in FY25.
Precast construction plant under way for captive use, technical support from Robin Village (Singapore); claimed benefits include about 30% lower material wastage and 40% lower workforce need.
Labour accommodation for about 500-plus workers under development at Rustomjee Balmoral, Chembur.
Cluster redevelopment projects: Seasons (about 168 members) and Elements, Andheri (about 480 members); GTB project is 11.5 acres, which may be developed in two phases.
Construction finance lines are in place; management says it has not needed to draw the full contracted amount in the past two years.
demand_pricing: Sales pattern: about 35% sold by plinth (first year), about 75% by sustenance stage, 15-20% during fit-out, 5-10% post OC. 66% of FY24 launches and 49% of FY25 launches already sold as of March 2026; 17% of FY26 launches sold in-year.
Unsold inventory about INR12,000 crore, of which about INR8,000 crore from FY25 launches; about 49% of total inventory sold.
Input costs up about 8-13% in certain items, roughly 5% overall; management says the 35%/40% sales pattern lets it reprice unsold stock.
Demand: no slowdown seen in premium and luxury; INR1-3 crore segment needs more push. Buying decisions taking longer.
Pipeline mix: about 94% of forthcoming pipeline in emerging premium to super premium. Large share of BD in INR1-3 crore and INR1-4 crore segments; affordable not targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Why are sold receivables low versus cost to complete on the residential book (Slide 30)?
qa_highlights.answer: Sajal Gupta said about INR8,000 crore of the INR12,000 crore unsold inventory comes from FY25 launches; 49% of total inventory is sold and sales follow a 35/40/15-20/5-10 pattern that funds cost to complete.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commercial annuity income target and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Boman Irani targets about INR100 crore by 2030, recovering costs via pre-leasing and sales to larger funds or HNIs while retaining some assets; commercial projects are about 60-65% sold to recover development cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash outflow for cluster versus single redevelopment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said equity investment stays about 10-11% of project GDV for cluster projects, with phased investment possible on very large sites like GTB.

qa_highlights.question: When do legacy projects end and what margin profile follows?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy projects are 62% of FY26 revenue and 12% in FY27; FY28 onward is expected at about 35% blended gross margin and 20% EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why is collection efficiency declining and what is the expected range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the lower ratio to a higher share of newly launched projects in presales; collection efficiency is expected at 75-80% from this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 peak debt and finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt is expected to peak at INR1,300-1,400 crore in FY27 (excluding commercial), with average debt of about INR1,000 crore and finance cost of about INR95 crore at 9.5%.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Middle East crisis and cost inflation affecting demand and input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: No slowdown in premium segment; INR1-3 crore segment needs more push. Input costs up about 5% overall, with supply shortages of imported materials creating delays.

risks_watch: Revenue recognition shift to POCM: FY27 mix is 60% POCM, so reported profit and cash flow may not track presales smoothly.
Collection efficiency guided lower at 75-80%, and sales pace in the INR1-3 crore segment needs more push.
Rising input costs (about 5% overall, 8-13% in some items) and import shortages could cause delays.
Debt rising from INR755 crore to INR1,300-1,400 crore in FY27 with the 0.75:1 D/E cap; commercial projects are debt-heavy.
Target of INR10,000 crore presales by FY30 requires about 26% CAGR; ROE/ROCE guidance not yet provided.
Bandstand Cama (27 apartments, about 30% sold) and the super-luxury redevelopment deal (to be announced around Q3 FY27) are pending updates.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, presales and balance sheet, with repeated references to meeting or beating guidance. Specifics became less firm on ROE/ROCE guidance (deferred), peak debt for FY28 (deferred), and super-luxury redevelopment (no names given).
key_quotes: We have always met or surpassed every single guidance metric that we have shared with you.
Each project is underwritten at approximately 35% gross margins with upfront equity capital capped at approximately 10% total project GDV.
So basically, I think we are probably one of the most well poised to take advantage of this entire growth.
So this INR100 crores estimate we are speaking about is based on the estimate of what we are going to retain into these projects.
